document_metadata.title: 1、INT DOCTOR'S OFFICE - DAY
document_metadata.summary: Hazel, a cancer survivor with an oxygen tank, rejects the idea that her depression stems from cancer, viewing it instead as a consequence of dying, and navigates daily life with quiet detachment.

entities.name: Hazel's mother expresses concern about her mental health to a doctor
entities.description: Hazel's mother, Frannie, tells a doctor that Hazel eats very little, rarely leaves the house, and reads the same book repeatedly, indicating her worry that Hazel is depressed.

entities.name: Hazel repeatedly denies being depressed
entities.description: While her mother speaks to the doctor, Hazel insists multiple times that she is not depressed, asserting her emotional state against their concerns.

entities.name: Doctor concludes Hazel is depressed
entities.description: After hearing Frannie's observations, the doctor makes a clinical judgment that Hazel is suffering from depression.

entities.name: Hazel Grace Lancaster
entities.description: A teenage girl with cancer who is self-aware and resistant to being labeled as depressed, despite her mother's concerns and the doctor's diagnosis.
entities.summary: A sarcastic, self-aware teenage girl undergoing cancer treatment resists her mother's concerns, medical labels, and pressure to attend support groups, showing disengagement from emotional discussions and social interactions while maintaining skepticism toward prescribed narratives.

document_metadata.title: 2、INT DOCTOR'S OFFICE - SAME
document_metadata.summary: Hazel resists attending a support group for depression, scoffing at the doctor's suggestion, while her mother confirms she's gone a few times. The doctor urges her to try it.

document_metadata.title: 74、INT VAN HOUTEN'S HOME - SAME
document_metadata.summary: Lidewij resigns; Van Houten insists Hazel and Gus leave, refusing to answer their questions. Hazel is furious, but Gus urges her to go, and they depart.

entities.name: Lidewij leads Gus and Hazel into Van Houten's living room
entities.description: Lidewij guides Gus and Hazel into a stark, minimally furnished living room where Van Houten is seated, marking the beginning of their visit.

entities.name: Van Houten acknowledges receiving fan mail but refuses to open it
entities.description: Van Houten reveals through gesture and dialogue that he has accumulated 18 years of unopened fan mail stored in garbage bags, indicating his disengagement from readers.

entities.name: Van Houten requests scotch and Lidewij serves him despite concerns
entities.description: Van Houten asks for a drink, Lidewij expresses concern about his drinking, compares it to believing in scientific facts, but ultimately pours him half a glass of scotch which he drinks.

entities.name: Hazel explains purpose of visit regarding Van Houten's book
entities.description: Hazel tells Van Houten that Augustus made meeting him his Wish, and they have come to ask questions about the fates of characters after the end of his novel.

entities.name: Van Houten questions Hazel about her clothing choice
entities.description: Van Houten asks Hazel if she dressed like a character from his book on purpose, making a pointed observation about her shirt.

entities.name: Van Houten denies having a drinking problem with a Churchill analogy
entities.description: Van Houten claims he does not have a drinking problem, instead describing a 'Churchillian relationship' with alcohol—able to function despite dependency—while Lidewij silently refills his glass.

entities.name: Gus thanks Van Houten for dinner from the previous night
entities.description: Augustus expresses gratitude for a meal provided the night before, prompting Van Houten to question whether they actually hosted it, with Lidewij confirming it was their pleasure.

entities.name: Van Houten reluctantly engages with visitors' questions
entities.description: After initial resistance and skepticism, Van Houten acknowledges the effort behind the visit and asks what he can do for Hazel and Gus, opening space for inquiry.

entities.name: Van Houten's living room
entities.description: A sparsely furnished, sterile living room where Van Houten receives guests, characterized by empty white walls and minimal furniture.

entities.name: Lidewij Vliegenthart
entities.description: A woman who assists Van Houten and interacts with Gus and Hazel during their visit, serving as a caretaker or companion figure.
entities.summary: Van Houten's assistant, a woman present during Hazel and Gus's visit, assists him, expresses discomfort at his behavior, prepares drinks, apologizes, and engages with the pair, later suggesting an outing and returning with elevator information.

entities.name: Gus
entities.description: A young man visiting Van Houten with Hazel, participating in the conversation about the book and its aftermath.
entities.summary: Augustus Waters, a charismatic cancer survivor and amputee, forms a deep, affectionate bond with Hazel, engaging in thoughtful dialogue about life, literature, and identity while using metaphors like unlit cigarettes to express complex emotions.

entities.name: Hazel Grace Lancaster
entities.description: A young woman who has read Van Houten's book and travels with Gus to meet him, seeking answers about the characters' fates after the story ends.
entities.summary: A sarcastic, self-aware teenage girl undergoing cancer treatment resists her mother's concerns, medical labels, and pressure to attend support groups, showing disengagement from emotional discussions and social interactions while maintaining skepticism toward prescribed narratives.

entities.name: Peter Van Houten
entities.description: A reclusive author who wrote a book that deeply affected Hazel and Gus; he receives them in his living room with reluctance and sarcasm.
entities.summary: A reclusive author, central to Hazel and Gus's journey, meets them reluctantly, dismisses their emotional concerns, and later attends Gus's funeral to deliver a message to Hazel, who resists engagement.

entities.name: two large black garbage bags
entities.description: Garbage bags filled with 18 years' worth of unopened fan mail addressed to Van Houten, symbolizing his detachment from his readers.

entities.name: scotch and soda
entities.description: An alcoholic drink requested by Van Houten and served by Lidewij, reflecting his drinking habits and contested relationship with alcohol.

entities.name: fan mail
entities.description: Letters sent by readers to Van Houten over 18 years, which he refuses to open, representing his disengagement from his audience.

entities.name: Van Houten interrupts to quiz Hazel and Gus on Swedish hip-hop
entities.description: Van Houten abruptly shifts the conversation to test Hazel and Gus's knowledge of Swedish hip-hop, specifically referencing Afasi Och Filthy's album "Flacken."

entities.name: Van Houten orders Lidewij to play 'Bomfalleralla'
entities.description: Van Houten commands Lidewij to immediately play the song 'Bomfalleralla' by Afasi Och Filthy, which she reluctantly complies with.

entities.name: Lidewij plays loud Swedish rap music despite visible annoyance
entities.description: Lidewij sighs but obeys Van Houten's order, playing a loud Swedish rap song that fills the room and bewilders Hazel and Gus.

entities.name: Hazel and Gus endure the music in confusion
entities.description: Hazel and Gus remain seated and attempt to tolerate the unfamiliar and jarring music, clearly disoriented by the situation.

entities.name: Hazel shouts apology over music due to language barrier
entities.description: Hazel yells to Van Houten that they don't speak Swedish, attempting to explain their inability to engage with the song.

entities.name: Van Houten declares emotional resonance over linguistic understanding
entities.description: Van Houten yells back that the meaning lies not in the words but in the emotional quality of the voices, dismissing the need to understand Swedish.

entities.name: Gus stands up and turns off the music in frustration
entities.description: After enduring the song for about ten seconds, Gus interrupts the music by turning it off, signaling his growing irritation.

entities.name: Gus confronts Van Houten about being mocked
entities.description: Gus challenges Van Houten, asking if he is being deliberately ridiculed through the music and behavior.

entities.name: Van Houten responds with philosophical justification referencing Rudolf Otto
entities.description: Van Houten deflects Gus's accusation by invoking Rudolf Otto's concept of the numinous, equating appreciation of his work with the ability to feel Afasi Och Filthy's emotional defiance.

entities.name: Hazel grows increasingly anxious about the purpose of the visit
entities.description: Hazel becomes visibly worried, doubting the value of their journey and questioning whether they will gain any meaningful insight from Van Houten.

entities.name: Hazel attempts to redirect conversation back to book's plot
entities.description: Hazel tries to refocus the discussion by bringing up the unresolved storyline concerning Anna's mother at the end of Van Houten's novel.

entities.description: Hazel and Gus stand with Lidewij among a group of backpackers and travelers preparing to begin a guided tour of the Anne Frank House.

entities.description: Lidewij points out the bookcase that concealed the entrance to the secret annex where the Frank family and four others hid during World War II.

entities.description: Despite physical difficulty, Hazel starts ascending the narrow, steep staircase behind the bookcase, moving slowly and with visible effort.

entities.name: Gus expresses concern about continuing the climb
entities.description: Gus looks at Hazel with hesitation, questioning whether they should proceed up the increasingly difficult staircase.

entities.name: Hazel struggles and rests on the next floor
entities.description: After reaching the next floor, Hazel leans against a wall, visibly exhausted and struggling to breathe, while Gus comforts her.

entities.name: Gus praises Hazel as a champion
entities.description: Gus reassures Hazel by telling her she's a champion, acknowledging her strength and determination during the difficult climb.

entities.name: Hazel continues to the final narrow staircase
entities.description: After a brief rest, Hazel and Gus enter another room containing an even steeper and narrower staircase, nearly a ladder, leading to the top level.

entities.name: Gus insists the climb should stop
entities.description: Upon seeing the final, extremely narrow staircase, Gus tells Hazel that they should go no further, out of concern for her health.

entities.name: Hazel resolutely climbs the final staircase
entities.description: Determined to continue, Hazel slowly and laboriously climbs the final steep and narrow staircase, struggling with every breath.

entities.name: Hazel stumbles and collapses at the top
entities.description: Near the top of the final staircase, Hazel stumbles but manages to pull herself through, then falls to the floor, slumped against the wall, gasping for breath.

entities.name: Gus reassures Hazel upon reaching the top
entities.description: Gus crouches beside Hazel at the top of the stairs and tells her they have made it, offering comfort and support.

entities.name: Tourists observe Hazel with concern
entities.description: Other tourists in the space notice Hazel's distress and watch her with quiet concern, murmuring in foreign languages.

entities.name: Hazel recovers and stands to downplay her struggle
entities.description: After catching her breath, Hazel stands up and smiles, signaling to the onlookers that she is fine and there is nothing to worry about.

document_metadata.title: 101、EXT CEMETARY - DAY
document_metadata.summary: Hazel, angry and grieving, demands Van Houten leave her car; he complies, stepping out as she drives away, seeing him toast her with his flask in the rearview mirror.

entities.name: Gus's body is lowered into the ground during the burial
entities.description: The funeral ceremony takes place as Gus's body is lowered into the grave, with attendees present except for Hazel and Van Houten.

entities.name: Hazel looks away from the burial into the distance
entities.description: During Gus's burial, Hazel avoids watching the coffin being lowered and instead gazes off into the distance, emotionally detached from the ceremony.

entities.name: Van Houten watches Hazel during the burial
entities.description: Instead of observing the burial, Van Houten stands to the side and silently watches Hazel, showing focused attention on her emotional state.

entities.name: Hazel reassures her parents after the ceremony
entities.description: After the funeral ends, Hazel tells her parents she will be fine and declines their offer for a ride, requesting time alone.

entities.name: Hazel hugs her parents before leaving
entities.description: Hazel embraces her mother and father in a farewell gesture before walking alone toward the parking lot.

entities.name: Van Houten asks Hazel for a ride
entities.description: As Hazel reaches her car, Van Houten approaches and requests a ride, initially only to the bottom of the hill.

entities.name: Hazel reluctantly agrees to give Van Houten a ride
entities.description: After a moment of hesitation and visible discomfort, Hazel agrees to let Van Houten ride with her.

entities.name: Van Houten reveals he came for the funeral to deliver a message
entities.description: In the car, Van Houten explains that Gus corresponded with him before his death and insisted he attend the funeral to tell Hazel what happened to Anna and her mother.

entities.name: Van Houten quotes 'omnis cellula e cellula' to Hazel
entities.description: Van Houten repeatedly references the Latin phrase 'omnis cellula e cellula', attempting to convey a philosophical or symbolic message to Hazel during the car ride.

entities.name: Hazel rejects Van Houten's attempt to explain further
entities.description: Hazel explicitly tells Van Houten she is not interested in hearing more, dismisses him, and ends the conversation.

entities.name: Hazel Grace Lancaster
entities.description: A young woman grieving the loss of Gus, who attends his funeral and later gives Van Houten a ride despite her reluctance.
entities.summary: A sarcastic, self-aware teenage girl undergoing cancer treatment resists her mother's concerns, medical labels, and pressure to attend support groups, showing disengagement from emotional discussions and social interactions while maintaining skepticism toward prescribed narratives.

entities.name: Peter Van Houten
entities.description: A reclusive author who attends Gus's funeral at his request and seeks to deliver a message to Hazel, though she resists engaging with him.
entities.summary: A reclusive author, central to Hazel and Gus's journey, meets them reluctantly, dismisses their emotional concerns, and later attends Gus's funeral to deliver a message to Hazel, who resists engagement.

entities.name: Gus
entities.description: A deceased young man whose funeral is the central event of the scene, remembered by Hazel and others.
entities.summary: Augustus Waters, a charismatic cancer survivor and amputee, forms a deep, affectionate bond with Hazel, engaging in thoughtful dialogue about life, literature, and identity while using metaphors like unlit cigarettes to express complex emotions.

entities.name: Frannie
entities.description: Hazel's mother, who expresses concern for her daughter after the funeral ceremony.
entities.summary: Hazel's mother, in her early 40s, is deeply concerned about her daughter's mental health, social withdrawal, and behavior, prompting her to seek medical input, attend support sessions, and encourage social interaction while showing authority and impatience.
